title: The purge that never propagated
blurb: Accepted meant done, and a wildcard purged the whole domain.
prompt: A pricing fix stayed broken on some edges for six hours because the draft marked the purge done at provider acceptance, and a normal-token wildcard purge hammered the origin into an outage. Review it, fix it, and prove status is honest and blast radius is gated.
aiNote: The draft reports done when the provider accepts the request, so propagation failures are invisible and on-call believes the cache is clean, and it lets a normal token request a domain-wide wildcard, turning one request into an origin stampede.
testIdea: Return partial failure from the provider and assert the status reports partially failed with paths; request a wildcard with a normal token and assert 403; retry a purge with the same key and assert the provider is called once.
followUps: When does a targeted purge beat a versioned URL?
How would you purge without knowing every path?
What budget keeps deploys from DDoSing the provider?
